answer: Memory-tithe decay curve: each identity accrues a small recurring charge that resets its standing only while it stays active; dormant or cloned identities slide down a terrace of reduced reach. Standing is a garden that must be watered: sustained activity yields compounding privileges, while mass-registered shells each pay the same upkeep with no shared benefit. An attacker running N identities pays linear maintenance on every one, and a walnut of collateral per identity is forfeited on lapse, so scaling N multiplies cost without multiplying influence.
